MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING

1.  In order to minimize the spread of the COVID- 19 Virus, Governor Newsom issued an Executive Order that
  Council Chambers was closed to the public, La Verne
  temporarily suspends requirements of the Brown Act. The
  City Council Members attended this meeting telephonically, and meeting was live streamed on the City' s website.

2.  A regular meeting of the La Verne City Council was called to order by Mayor Hepburn at 6: 32 pm
3.  Council Members present:  Mayor Tim Hepburn
  Mayor Pro Tem Robin Carder
  Council Member Muir Davis
  Council Member Wendy Lau
  Council Member Rick Crosby

  Services Navigator  Mental Health Center and Union Station Homeless Services introduced their
  Introductions  and Presentation  Navigators to the City Council  The Navigators specialize in providing
  resources, services,  and outreach  to individuals experiencing, or on the cusp
  of experiencing, homelessness.  The Navigators were hired through grant
  funds awarded  as part of the  County of Los Angeles' 2018 Cities
  Homelessness  Plan Implementation  Program,  and are a critical part of the

  City' s strategic efforts to prevent and address
  homelessness.  They spoke
  about the work they do in La Verne along with a slide presentation.

  There was no public comment on this matter.

  Homeless  Plan  Annual  Review  Homele  s  Plan  Annual  Review-  On June 18, 2018 the City Council
  approved Resolution No. 18- 33, adopting the City' s" Plan to Prevent and
  Reduce  Homelessness"(  Homeless  Plan).  The adopted  Homeless  Plan
  outlines four( 4) strategic goals, along with supporting action items, to prevent
  and reduce homelessness over the course of three( 3) years. Action item 4b
  identifies that the Homeless Plan should be reviewed on an annual basis at a
  time corresponding with, or after, the release of the most recent annual Point
  in Time Homeless Count results. This staff report summarizes the progress
  that has occurred since the last progress report was provided to City Council in
  July 2019.

  Community Development Director Scherer recommended that the City Council
  receive  and  file this  informational  report.  Report received and filed by

  Mayor Hepburn opened the public hearing, called for public comment on this
  matter, and waited for staff to check.

  There was none.

  The Council all agreed that it was good step enacting the ordinance which
  would protect residents, participates, and law enforcement at all public
  demonstrations.

  It was moved by Davis, seconded by Crosby and unanimously carried to
  waive further reading and place on first reading Ordinance No. 1097,
  amending Title 9 of the La Verne Municipal Code by adding a new Section
  9. 21. 00 ( b) to regulate the possession of certain items that may cause harm to
  the community, participates, and law enforcement at public protests,
  demonstrations, rallies, picket lines, and public assemblies.

 8.  Public Comment  This was the time set aside for anyone wishing to address the City Council on
  items not listed in any other place  on  the agenda.  Mayor Hepburn called for
  public comment and waited for staff to check for any public comment via
  telephone  communication.

  There was  none and  no public  comments received  by email.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, October 19, 2020, Page 4

9.  Council  Comments  Mayor Pro Tem Carder stated that with two weeks before Halloween there are
  many events going on in La Verne. She reported on the Gold Line
  Construction and reminded everyone that Wheeler Avenue at the railroad
  October 13, 2020
  crossing north of Arrow Highway is closed which started on
  through January 1 , 2021 .

  Council Member Davis reported on the Pomona Valley Transportation
  Committee  meeting. He stated that they are still providing local Get About
  service  at no fee during the COVID- 19 pandemic.  He also reported on the
  Public Bank Pomona  Valley meeting ( A California Public Banking Alliance).
  He reminded everyone that it' s flu season and to get your flu shot.

  Council Member Lau wished everyone a Happy Halloween and announced
  that October is Breast Cancer and Domestic Violence awareness month.

  Council Member Crosby spoke about the importance of testing for breast
  cancer. He urged the community to VOTE and there are two authorized Los
  Angeles County Ballot Boxes one at the La Verne Library and the other at Oak
  Mesa Park.  He spoke about redistricting and needing more information on the
  matter for a future  Council meeting.  He wished everyone a safe Halloween.

  Mayor Hepburn  thanked the Council for their comments.  He too,
  acknowledged  Breast Cancer  and  Domestic Violence  awareness month.  He
  urged everyone  to check on family and friends.  He announced  he was elected
  Second President to the San Gabriel Valley Council  of Governments.  He
  spoke about a proposed bill they are looking at that would protect City rights.
  He asked everyone to keep the Armenian people in their prayers and spoke
  about  the  recent  demostration  march  by the group. He thanked Police Chief
  Paz and his officers for keeping the participants and the community safe
  during the march. He urged everyone to shop La Verne and to dine in
  La Verne.  He wished everyone a Happy Halloween.
